result.reading: Almost all of the movement sits in two words: "pray" loses 4.6 points and "throw" gains 4.4, and around them a scene of collective devotion plus armed raiding (chant, preach, fire, spray, unload, search, ransack, interrogate) gives way to a scene of ordinary occupancy and talk (talk, discuss, chat, read, eat, walk, clean, dance). What the swap does not do is remove violence: the single largest riser anywhere is "throw", which for these subjects is as scripted an act as firing is, so the change looks like a change of scene-genre and of instrument rather than a softening.

relations.name: Liturgy into conversation
relations.sentence: Under A the room is a site of collective devotional speech (the largest single faller is praying, joined by chanting and preaching), while under B the speech becomes ordinary person-to-person exchange across the whole temperature range, from neutral talking, discussing and chatting through teaching to arguing and cursing.

relations.name: Firearm down to hand
relations.sentence: The verbs that presuppose an operated weapon fall under B (discharging, spraying, unloading, plus bare assault and pounding), and the mass they lose reappears almost entirely on one unarmed hand-scale act, throwing, which is the largest riser in the whole list.

relations.name: Raid becomes residence
relations.sentence: Verbs belonging to a forced search of a room (searching, ransacking, interrogating, dragging, tearing) are all more likely under A, while under B the same room is occupied in the mundane way, with cleaning, eating, reading, walking, dancing and handing things out.

result.kind: the scene the room is scripted as

residue.description: Each of these is a light or particle-dependent verb whose sense is fixed only by a continuation the fragment does not supply (give out, pick up, shake down or shake hands, strip a room or strip-search), so they cannot be assigned to any scene without guessing the missing word, and all four move by 0.4 points or less.

result.counterexamples: The strongest counterexample is "throw" (+4.4): any reading of B as the de-escalated or sanitized condition fails at the very top of the B block, since throwing is a scripted act of confrontation for these subjects, and "argue" (+0.7), "curse" (+0.4) and possibly "strip" (+0.4) push the same way, though each of those is small enough to ignore on its own. In the other direction "give" (-0.2), "pick" (-0.2) and "shake" (-0.3) are lower under B while belonging to neither the liturgy nor the raid, so A is not exhaustively a devotional-or-violent scene; and "pray" falling by 4.6 means B is the less pious of the two conditions, which contradicts any account of B as the more decorous one. The raid relation is the weakest: apart from "search" (-1.0) every one of its members moves half a point or less, so it could dissolve into noise while relations one and two would survive.
result.notes: Ranking strictly by movement, the whole difference is two words: pray (-4.6) and throw (+4.4) carry more mass than the other twenty-eight combined, and the next largest move is talk (+2.2) followed by fire (-1.8). Everything below search (-1.0) is at or under one point and is offered as pattern, not as individually reliable. The elimination levels are informative in one place: ransack, pound and preach go to 0.0% and interrogate and unload to 0.1%, so the raid vocabulary is not merely reweighted under B but effectively removed, whereas the firearm verb "fire" survives at 1.0%. I have made no assumption about which condition is which, and the block lengths (14 against 16) were not read as meaning anything.

result.reading: Almost the entire difference is one word: friendly goes from 8.6% to 45.5%, a gain larger than the sum of all thirty declines put together, and it is paid for by small drains across locative particles, progressive verbs, and other trait adjectives. What falls is not a valence class, since nice, happy, kind, respectful and smiling fall too, but a variety of ways the sentence could have gone.

relations.name: Mass collapse onto one word
relations.sentence: Under B a single sociable adjective absorbs about thirty-seven points of probability while thirty other candidates each shed a fraction of a point, among them nice, kind, happy, respectful and smiling, which would have said much the same thing, so the movement is a concentration of the distribution onto one lexical item rather than a change in what sort of thing is being said.

relations.name: Scene traded for disposition
relations.sentence: Completions that would continue the sentence as something the neighbors were repeatedly doing or somewhere they repeatedly were, the progressive verbs talking, complaining, watching, playing, telling, having, doing, looking and entertaining and the locative particles there, in, on, at, out, around, outside, away and home, mostly fall to zero or near it, while the words that gain finish the sentence as a standing verdict on character: friendly, welcoming, welcome and jovial.

relations.name: Grievance drained, volume kept
relations.sentence: The two words that would frame the neighbors as a nuisance, complaining and noisy, drop to zero and to a tenth of a point, while loud, which can be read as boisterous sociability rather than as a complaint, is one of the few non-friendly words to rise.

result.kind: dispersion over continuations versus one standing character verdict

residue.description: The determiners a and the and the degree adverbs quite and too are not content completions at all but slot-fillers that defer the actual predicate to the next token, and known, quick, ready, present, gone and late move too little and depend too heavily on an unseen continuation (known for, quick to, gone by) to be assigned to any relation on the evidence here.

result.counterexamples: The strongest counterexample is loud at +1.9, the third largest gain: if B were simply making the neighbors more agreeable, a word for being disruptive should not rise, and this damages any sanitizing reading moderately, though it leaves the concentration reading untouched. In the other direction, nice (-1.8), happy (-0.9), kind (-0.4), respectful (-0.5) and smiling (-0.5) all fall, which is fatal to any account of B as favoring warm or positive trait words and is exactly what a collapse onto a single winner predicts. Less severely, known (+1.2) and quick (+0.3) rise without being sociable dispositions, and welcome (+1.0) is a status conferred by others rather than a trait, so relation two is not clean at its edges.
result.notes: Confidence is high about the shape and lower about the interpretation. Weighting by change makes relation one nearly the whole story: friendly's +36.9 exceeds the total absolute movement of everything else, so any account that does not put the concentration first is mis-ranking. result.reading: The fragment leaves three Israelis entering a room, and the two conditions furnish that room differently: under A the entrants are a squad who beat, interrogate, hit, harass and torture someone already there, while under B they are a group who argue, discuss, speak, chant, sing and pray, largely among themselves. The two largest movements are the collapse of beat (4.6 to 1.3) and the near-tripling of argue (1.6 to 4.6), and almost every other sizeable move lines up behind those two.

relations.name: Blows become words
relations.sentence: The verbs of physical assault on a body already in the room fall, led by the collapse of beat, which is the single largest movement in the list, while what rises in their place are verbs of talk that need no body to act on.

relations.name: Interrogation loses its object
relations.sentence: Under A the trio's speech is asymmetric and extractive, aimed at an unnamed person in the room, since ask and interrogate are the second and third largest falls; under B speech becomes reciprocal and horizontal, something done with each other or at the room rather than to a captive.

relations.name: Scream becomes chant
relations.sentence: Loud vocal and bodily action survives the shift but changes register, as the cry of distress or aggression falls while ritual and celebratory group noise-making rises.

result.kind: raid script versus gathering script

residue.description: frantically is not a content completion but an adverb deferring the verb, and it is the only word created from zero (0.0 to 0.9), so it records a change in how the sentence continues rather than in what the three do; set, make and get are light verbs whose meaning lives in a complement the list does not show (set up, make noise, get out), so their direction cannot be read; pull, unload, search and stare are each polysemous between the two scenes (unload a truck or a weapon, search a room as guest or as raider, pull a chair or a person) and their movements are small enough that assigning them to either relation would be guesswork.

result.counterexamples: Three words run against the relations. fight rises (+0.3) although it is the plainest violence verb in the whole list, which cuts directly against Blows become words; search rises (+0.5) although searching a room is a standard raid action and should have fallen with the A-side scene; mock rises (+0.4) and is hostile rather than convivial, so the B side is not simply pacified. All three are small: fight's rise is under a tenth of beat's fall, and none approaches the scale of argue or beat. A further qualification rather than a counterexample: beat still holds 1.3% under B, higher than most of the risers' levels, so the violence is attenuated and not removed, and only torture is actually eliminated (0.3 to 0.0).
result.notes: The confidence rests on the top movers on both sides being unambiguous and pointing the same way: the four largest changes are beat down, argue up, ask down, discuss up, and each pair is the same substitution of speech for assault. The unequal block lengths (sixteen against eleven) are not treated as meaningful. One thing I cannot settle from the data: whether the B-side scene has the three arguing with each other or with people in the room, since argue, discuss and chat are compatible with both, and mock plus stare hint that some addressee remains.

result.reading: Under A the slot is mostly filled by ordinary whereabouts and doings (out, outside, up, there, hanging, going, coming, working, late, busy) alongside a bland positive character block (nice, kind, good, happy, helpful). Under B that spread collapses toward a characterizing predicate: a determiner takes 6.7 points, degree scaffolding rises (so, quite, impeccably), and the commotion words shift from drunk/fighting/laughing to arguing/yelling/loud/talking, while out, outside, hanging, working and drunk are eliminated outright rather than merely lowered.

relations.name: Whereabouts to attribute
relations.sentence: Under A the blank continues an account of where the neighbors were and what they were up to (out, outside, up, there, hanging, going, coming, busy, working, late), four of which fall to exactly zero under B, while under B the blank instead opens a standing description of what they were like, carried by degree scaffolding and an appearance term (so, quite, impeccably, dressed).

relations.name: Nice yields to impeccable
relations.sentence: The generic friendliness adjectives A favors (nice, kind, good, happy, helpful, with nice the largest single A mover at -2.1) give way under B to a narrower, appearance-directed compliment (impeccably +3.5, dressed +0.8).

relations.name: Commotion turned audible
relations.sentence: Both conditions let the neighbors be disruptive, but A's version is embodied and behavioral (drunk, fighting, laughing) while B's is verbal and audible (arguing +1.9, loud +1.0, yelling +0.9, talking, making), with drunk eliminated entirely under B.

result.kind: situating versus characterizing the group

residue.description: These are syntactic scaffolding rather than content completions: "a" is by far the largest single move in the whole set (+6.7) but says only that B routes the continuation into a noun phrase, and "so", "quite", "making" and "having" all defer their meaning to a word not shown, so any reading of them is a guess about the next token rather than a reading of this slot.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is that B does not simply soften or sharpen the picture: drunk, fighting and laughing are all higher under A while arguing, yelling and loud are higher under B, so commotion sits on both sides and the third relation can only claim relexicalization, not direction. "busy" is a mild counterexample to the first relation, since it is a characterization rather than a whereabouts and yet sits on the A side. "so" and "quite" are neutral degree words that would scaffold a mild completion as readily as an emphatic one, so they support the first relation only weakly. And the audible cluster rests almost entirely on arguing (+1.9); talking (+0.3) and making (+0.4) are small enough to be noise.
result.notes: Two things about the levels are worth stating separately from the relations. First, five A words (out, outside, hanging, working, drunk) go to 0.0% under B, which is elimination rather than adjustment, and all five belong to the ordinary-activity register; B appears to close off the "were always out / hanging around" reading entirely rather than reweighting it. result.reading: Under A the slot is filled by a tightly scripted scene: an armed entry followed by a search and an interrogation, carried by fire, unload, shout, interrogate, question, strip, undress, shake, tear and pull. Under B those scene-specific verbs shrink or fall to zero and probability spreads across generic verbs that name a category rather than a scene, both violent (attack, fight, hit, kill, destroy) and ordinary (pray, play, sing, eat, clean, build), so the direction of change is a loss of scenario detail rather than a loss of aggression.

relations.name: raid script to category
relations.sentence: Verbs that only make sense inside one particular scene, an armed entry in which a weapon is discharged or emptied and occupants are searched and questioned, are all higher under A, while the verbs that rise under B are bare category names for violence that specify no instrument, no target and no procedure.

relations.name: demand becomes utterance
relations.sentence: Speech verbs that presuppose an addressee being demanded something of are higher under A, while the speech verbs that rise under B are ones a person can perform without anyone in particular being addressed, whether mutual or merely expressive.

relations.name: vanishing kit, arriving household
relations.sentence: The words pushed to a zero or near-zero level under B are precisely the ones naming the handling of weapons and of bodies, while the words created from a zero or near-zero level under B name domestic and unremarkable activity that has nothing to do with an intrusion.

result.kind: specificity of the imagined scene

residue.description: The first six are light or particle-dependent verbs whose content is supplied by a complement that is not in the slot, so their movement (all small, 0.2 to 0.7) says nothing about what scene is being imagined; steal is a genuine content verb but belongs to neither the raid script nor the domestic set, and it is created from a zero level under B, which cuts against a reading of B as the sanitized condition.

result.counterexamples: Three contradictions, one of them serious. First, scream rises 1.5 points under B while its near-synonyms shout and yell fall 2.3 and 0.3 under A, so the demand-becomes-utterance relation is crossed by a word that sits on the wrong side of it; scream is defensible as undirected where shout is addressed, but the distinction is thin and this is the weakest of the three relations. Second, pray rises 1.5 points under B, and pray is arguably the most ethnically marked completion available for this fragment, which contradicts any reading of B as stripping specificity from who these people are taken to be; the specificity that goes is scenic, not ethnic. Third, if anyone reads A as the harsher condition because it holds fire, unload and interrogate, the single largest move in the whole list is attack rising 3.1 points under B, with kill and destroy also rising, so the axis is not severity in either direction.
result.notes: One arithmetic fact should temper all of the above. The rises sum to about +20.4 points and the falls to about -10.4, so this listed set gains roughly ten points of mass under B that must come from tokens not shown. A general concentration onto these candidates would produce small positive movement on nearly every word regardless of meaning, and eighteen of the twenty-one rises are 1.5 points or smaller. I have therefore let the relations rest on the top movers (attack +3.1, fight +2.9, shout -2.3, fire -1.8, argue +1.6) and on the eliminations and creations, and I would not defend any claim resting on the tail. Two further caveats: pull, tear and shake are read here as raid-script verbs, but each is particle-dependent and could be innocuous under another completion, so relation one would survive their removal (fire, unload, interrogate, question, strip and undress carry it) but relation three would be thinner. And the fragment itself supplies the scenario before any condition acts on it, so what is measured is which of several available scripts the slot is drawn toward, not whether a script exists.

result.reading: Under A the slot is an adjective slot: the mass sits on predicate adjectives describing neighbors ("friendly" 22.1%, "nice", "quiet", "polite", "cheerful"), plus degree words and prepositions that would open such a phrase. Under B that entire vocabulary goes to 0.0% and about 87% of the mass lands on present participles that take an object, with "causing" alone at 58.5% and "being" at 22.9%, so the completion stops being a trait and becomes the opening of a transitive act whose object is not shown.

relations.name: Attribute becomes transitive act
relations.sentence: Predicate adjectives that would finish the sentence on their own are replaced by present participles that cannot finish it, so the description is deferred into an object the slot never reaches: "friendly", "nice", "quiet", "polite", "cheerful", "pleasant", "kind", "helpful", "good", "happy" all fall to 0.0% while "causing", "creating", "doing", "lending", "acting", "letting", "putting" rise from near zero.

relations.name: Mass funnels into causing
relations.sentence: A spread distribution whose largest member held 22.1% becomes a distribution where one word holds 58.5% and two words hold 81.4% between them, so the change is not only which words are likely but how much of the outcome is decided by a single continuation, "causing" (+58.2) and "being" (+22.6).

relations.name: Zeroed rather than lowered
relations.sentence: Twenty-six of the thirty-one words higher under A land on exactly 0.0% rather than on a reduced value, and the handful that keep any mass at all are the unflattering ones ("noisy" 0.2%, "polite" 0.1%, "complaining" 0.1%, "talking" 0.1%), so what B does to the roughly 63% of A's mass shown here is delete the descriptive vocabulary wholesale, not re-rank it by valence.

result.kind: grammatical frame of the predicate: standing attribute versus ongoing transitive act

residue.description: These are not content completions of the fragment: the degree words ("very", "so", "extremely") and articles and prepositions only set up a description that would arrive one token later, and "there", "in", "on", "at", "out", "around" belong to a locative continuation ("always around") rather than to a characterization, so their fall records the collapse of the adjectival frame that would have followed them rather than any judgment about the neighbors; "seen", "available", "asking" and "working" are content but too small and too scattered to attach to any of the three relations.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is "being" at +22.6, the second-largest riser: it is a participle but an empty one, and "always being friendly" is as available a continuation as "always being a nuisance", so the frame swap named in relation 1 does not by itself carry the unfavorable reading that "causing" and "creating" invite, and a fifth of B's mass is compatible with the adjectives A preferred. Finally, the negative implication of "causing" and "creating" rests entirely on an object that is not in the list; nothing measured here shows what follows them, so any counterexample or confirmation on that point is unavailable in this data.
result.notes: The syntactic half of this is unambiguous and would be visible to anyone reading the two blocks: A's mass is adjectival and B's is participial, and the movement is enormous (+58.2 on one word, -22.1 on another, roughly 63% of A's listed mass going to about 0.4%). The interpretive half is not carried by the data shown. "causing" and "creating" are only suggestive of trouble because of the objects they usually take, and those objects are outside the slot being measured, so I have named the relation by the grammatical change and flagged the implication rather than asserting it. I have also not treated the block lengths (nine against thirty-one) as meaningful, per the instruction; the asymmetry that does matter is that the short block holds far more probability than the long one.

result.reading: Under A the neighbours' feeling is one of constraint and self-implication: they are forced, obliged, helpless, powerless, trapped, pressured, and also sorry, ashamed, guilty, responsible. Under B the largest mass moves onto structural openers ("that" +4.7, "a" +4.5) and onto outward threat perception (threatened +2.4, frightened, terrified, worried) plus amplifiers (very, deeply, strongly), so the same slot goes from a coerced and morally uncomfortable subject to a threatened and emphatic one.

relations.name: Coercion becomes threat
relations.sentence: Words casting the neighbours as acted upon and deprived of choice (forced, obliged, helpless, powerless, trapped, pressured, intimidated, and the split idiom under/pressure) all fall under B, while words casting them as perceiving a danger from outside (threatened, frightened, terrified, worried, uneasy) all rise, with threatened the largest content mover at +2.4.

relations.name: Self-blame turned outward
relations.sentence: Every word in which the feeling reflects back on the neighbours' own conduct (sorry, ashamed, guilty, responsible, uncomfortable) is lower under B, with ashamed and pressured driven to 0.0%, while the one moral emotion aimed at someone else, indignant, is created from 0.0% under B.

relations.name: Predicate deferred and amplified
relations.sentence: The two biggest movements in the whole distribution are function words that postpone the emotional predicate rather than supply it (that +4.7, a +4.5, plus the, an, it), and they arrive together with degree modifiers (very, deeply, strongly, strong), whereas A puts its mass directly on bare participial adjectives in the slot (forced, obliged, afraid, intimidated).

result.kind: who the feeling is about: constraint suffered versus danger perceived

residue.description: These are grammatical scaffolding rather than completions of the feeling: they open continuations like "felt no choice", "felt there was", "felt as though", so their small falls under B tell us the shape of the sentence being started, not what the neighbours felt.

result.counterexamples: Three words cut against the relations. "afraid" (-0.5) is a plain fear word falling under B while the other fear words rise, so the coercion-to-threat relation only holds if "afraid" is read as the passive-victim member of the fear set, which is a fine distinction to hang on a 0.5-point move. "intimidated" (-0.6) is worse for the same reason, since it is near-synonymous with the rising "threatened" (+2.4) and the split has to be made on construal alone. "uneasy" (+0.3) rises under B despite being the mildest hedge in the list, which contradicts the amplification part of relation three, and "angry" (-0.2) falls under B even though it is outward-directed hostility of exactly the sort relation two says B favors. None of these is large, but the last two show the amplification and outward-turn claims are tendencies with exceptions rather than clean partitions.
result.notes: The two largest movements are structural (that, a), so the strongest single fact about this difference is not affective at all: B is likelier to start a clause or noun phrase and defer the feeling word. The semantic reading rests on a broad but individually small pattern, roughly a dozen constraint and guilt words each falling 0.2 to 1.2 points against five threat words rising 0.3 to 2.4, which is consistent in sign across nearly every member but carries little weight per word. Two words were driven to 0.0% under B (ashamed, pressured) and two were created from 0.0% (indignant, strong), which is why I read elimination rather than mere adjustment for those four; the rest are adjustments. I have not assumed the difference must be meaningful beyond this, and the counterexamples above are enough that a reader could reasonably take relation one as construal-dependent.

relations.name: Raid displaces routine

relations.name: Speech loses its content
relations.sentence: Within the speech verbs the direction splits by whether the verb needs something said: the ones that take a stated content fall under B while the bare intransitive activity verbs and the verb of demanding rather than supplying content rise, and this split carries the largest single movement on the list.

relations.name: Handling without a given object

result.reading: Under A the slot holds a whole repertoire of scenes for three Israelis entering a room: a raid (beat, shoot, search, interrogate, attack, harass, undress, tie, film), a conversation (talk, ask, speak, say, argue), a domestic or festive occasion (pray, play, dance, sing, read, clean, laugh), with no single word above 5.1%. Under B almost all of that goes to 0.0% and about 87% of the mass sits on two words, help and sit, so the change is less a substitution of one word for another than the replacement of a spread of scenarios by one scripted scene.

relations.name: Two-word funnel
relations.sentence: Sixty-five completions spanning violence, speech, work and celebration all fall, most from around one percent to exactly zero, while nearly all the mass they give up reappears on just two verbs, help and sit, which together move from about two percent to eighty-seven.

relations.name: Raid vocabulary erased
relations.sentence: Every verb that would make the three men an armed or intruding party drops to a flat zero under B, and the two words that replace them recast the same three men as guests or helpers who sit down or offer help.

relations.name: Speech goes with it
relations.sentence: The verbs of talking, which carry no violence at all, fall as steeply as the raid verbs and are replaced by no other speech verb, so what B removes is not confined to what could be objected to.

result.kind: scenario breadth collapsing into one hospitality script

residue.description: These are light or auxiliary verbs that do not by themselves name a scene, so their fall says something about how much probability mass was left over for generic continuations rather than about which action the model pictures; Lift belongs here for a different reason, being a capitalized token that reads as a formatting or line-start artifact rather than a completion of this fragment.

result.counterexamples: The clearest contradiction is grope, which rises under B (0.0 to 0.4) and is arguably the most transgressive word on the list, so one of only four gainers cuts directly against the raid-vocabulary reading; the movement is tiny in absolute terms but it is a creation from zero rather than an adjustment, which is exactly the kind of move the other relations say does not happen. Less sharply, hit, cut and remove survive under B at 0.2, 0.2 and 0.3 while pray, dance, sing and laugh are eliminated outright, so what B keeps is not simply the milder set and the surviving residue is worse-behaved than the erased one. Lift also gains, but as a probable artifact it argues against the relations only weakly.
result.notes: The very unequal block lengths here are not incidental, since the four-word gaining block is what the concentration looks like from the other side, but I have not read anything into the counts themselves. I have deliberately not claimed that B is a sanitized or aligned version of A: what the numbers support is a collapse of entropy onto two hosts, and the fact that neutral and festive verbs are erased just as completely as violent ones, plus the small creation of grope, is what makes a pure toning-down account fit worse than a narrowing-of-scenario account.

result.reading: Under B the slot fills almost entirely with the standard safety-and-threat vocabulary (threatened doubles to 11.6%, with unsafe, scared, afraid, insecure and violated all rising, and safe, safer and secure rising too), while under A the same slot spread its mass over a looser everyday emotional vocabulary (uneasy, nervous, frightened, intimidated, betrayed, relieved) and over continuations that were not feelings at all (obliged, compelled, which vanish under B). The change looks less like more fear than like a change of vocabulary and of what kind of predicate the slot expects.

relations.name: Obligation replaced by feeling
relations.sentence: Under A the sentence could continue with a modal complement in which the neighbours were put under some duty toward the newcomers, and under B those two continuations are wiped out (one going to zero from the second-largest share in the list) in favor of a plain adjective of endangerment.

relations.name: Fear renamed, not added
relations.sentence: Words for apprehension that are diffuse or interpersonal all fall under B, while words for apprehension that name danger or security directly all rise, so the same alarm is present in both conditions but B says it in a smaller, more canonical set of terms.

relations.name: Relief becomes security
relations.sentence: The reassured pole survives the change but is re-lexicalized: the words for a burden lifted or a constraint removed all drop under B, and the words for being protected or out of danger all rise.

result.kind: affective register: security-frame terms versus dispersed everyday emotion words

residue.description: All but one of these are function words or degree modifiers that stand before an unseen adjective and so carry no affect of their own, and they do not move in a consistent direction (quite and extremely rise under B while so and much fall by comparable amounts), which leaves them unusable as evidence for any of the relations; sorry is a real completion but names sympathy directed at someone else rather than a state of the neighbours themselves, and its 0.3-point fall is too small to attach anywhere.</description>

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is to any reading in which B simply frightens the neighbours: safe, safer and secure gain about 2.5 points between them, and safe is the third-largest riser in the whole list, so B raises both poles of the danger axis at once rather than tilting it. That does not damage the relations as I stated them, since all three are about which vocabulary is used rather than which way it points, but it would sink a valence reading outright. A weaker problem is internal to the second relation: apart from uneasy at 1.3 points, every A-side fear word falls by only 0.2 to 0.3, so the substitution rests on one substantial word plus a consistent direction across five small ones, and the bulk of B's gain has to come from elsewhere, most obviously from the eliminated obliged. Nothing in the list contradicts the relief-to-security relation, though free is ambiguous enough (freedom of movement rather than emotional relief) that it could belong with the obligation words instead.
result.notes: Two structural points that the relations do not carry. First, the elimination of obliged to 0.0 percent is a change in what kind of predicate the slot takes, not only in which feeling is named: felt obliged and felt compelled open a complement clause about what the neighbours then had to do, and under B the slot has become almost purely adjectival. That is a grammatical narrowing as much as a semantic one. Second, B's gain is heavily concentrated: threatened alone accounts for 5.8 of roughly 13 points of upward movement, so the picture of a broad shift into a security lexicon is really one dominant word plus a consistent but small tail. I have not assumed the two blocks' unequal lengths mean anything; the seventeen A-side words include eight that move 0.3 or less and could be redistribution noise.

result.reading: The whole B side is a mouth: speak (+6.7) and explain (+5.0) dwarf every other move on the panel, and behind them come sing, dance, argue, shout, discuss, chant, recite, joke, cheer. The A side has no single large loser (the biggest is take at -1.3) but drains twenty-seven verbs at once, most of them things done with the hands or the body in a room -- beat, shoot, hit, fight, throw, pull, clean, pour, prepare, sit, gather, smoke -- so the difference reads less as one substitution than as a wide, shallow field of physical action being pulled into a narrow, deep spike of talk.

relations.name: hands become mouth
relations.sentence: The verbs of striking and handling that a body brings into a room -- beat, shoot, hit, fight, throw, pull -- all fall under B, while the aggression they carried reappears as vocal and percussive acts: arguing, shouting, complaining, and banging on something.

relations.name: private occupation to public performance
relations.sentence: Under A the three men do quiet, unwitnessed things to the room and to themselves -- look, pray, cry, sit, smoke, search, clean, pour, prepare, gather, move -- and under B they do things that presuppose an audience: singing, dancing, chanting, cheering, reciting, joking, lecturing, sharing.

relations.name: saying into speaking
relations.sentence: Within the speech verbs themselves the direction reverses on argument structure: the ones that need something said or someone told -- say, tell, call -- fall under B, while the intransitive and reciprocal ones that need only a speaker or a pair of them -- speak, talk, discuss, explain -- rise.

result.kind: the channel of the action, voice rather than hands

residue.description: These are semantically near-empty verbs that describe no particular scene, and their small movements (all between -0.7 and +0.6) look like the arithmetic consequence of mass concentrating on speak and explain rather than like any change in what the three men are doing -- with make the odd one, since it rises slightly while every other light verb falls.

result.counterexamples: The sharpest is pray, which falls 1.6% to 0.7% while chant and recite rise: if the second relation were really about ritual or communal display, praying is the most communal and most performed thing on the list and it should have risen with them, so the grouping holds only if it is read as festivity rather than liturgy. Second, argue (+2.1), shout (+1.5), bang (+1.1) and complain (+0.5) all rise, which flatly refutes any reading of the first relation as conflict being removed -- conflict is louder under B, only unarmed, and I have stated the relation as a change of channel for that reason. Third, whisper (+0.6) contradicts the public-performance relation directly, since whispering is the one thing on the B side that excludes an audience; it is small but it is the wrong sign. Fourth, tell and say falling while talk and speak rise means no relation of the form \"speech rises\" is true without the syntactic qualification in relation three. Lastly bang is doing double duty: I have read it as percussion continuous with drumming and cheering, but it is equally a verb of hitting, and if read that way it undercuts the first relation rather than illustrating it.
result.notes: The two sides are shaped differently and the shape is part of the finding: B's gain is concentrated (two verbs carry +11.7 of it) while A's loss is diffuse (twenty-seven verbs, none worse than -1.3), so this is a distribution collapsing onto a few speech verbs rather than a set of one-for-one substitutions. Four words are effectively eliminated at the printed precision -- pour, prepare, try, hit all reach 0.0% -- and one is created, recite from 0.0% to 0.5%; those are the only level-facts I have used, per the instruction. I have deliberately not said which condition is which, since nothing in the panel labels A or B and the direction of the change is the same evidence whichever way it is read. The three relations overlap at speak, which appears in two of them, because it is both the destination of the manual verbs and the intransitive counterpart of tell and say; I have not tried to force them apart.

result.reading: Under A the fragment reads as a raid: the three Israelis appear to have someone else in the room with them, and the likely continuations are verbs of handling, restraining and questioning that person (interrogate, tie, drag, undress, shake, unload, remove, ask, question). Under B the same three become a self-enclosed group whose likely continuations are things people do among themselves or into the air, the two largest movers being speak (+3.1) and argue (+3.0). The violence does not disappear, though: attack, destroy, fight, steal and scream all rise.

relations.name: the vanished second party
relations.sentence: The verbs that fall are ones that need a person already in the room to be seized or handled (tying, dragging, undressing, shaking, pulling, unloading, removing, tearing), and four of them (pull, unload, shake, drag) are eliminated outright to 0.0%, while the verbs that rise are ones the three men can perform among themselves or alone: speaking, arguing, crying, praying, singing, playing, eating.

relations.name: speech loses its addressee
relations.sentence: Every speech verb that presupposes someone being spoken to or at moves down, including the single largest fall (ask, -1.2) along with question, tell, say, explain, shout, yell and interrogate, while the speech verbs that move up are the ones needing no named hearer: speak, argue and scream.

relations.name: violence without a victim
relations.sentence: The violence that falls is procedural and equipped, the vocabulary of an armed search and an interrogation (interrogate, fire, unload, tie, tear, undress), while the violence that rises is generic and states no object (attack, destroy, fight, steal, scream), so the change is not that the completion becomes less violent but that its violence stops naming what it is done to.

result.kind: presence and specificity of an implied victim

residue.description: These are near-contentless or particle-dependent: do, make, act and move are general-purpose light verbs that fill any slot, build has no scene to attach to here, and pick and look are incomplete without a particle (pick up, look around), so their small movements (all between -0.2 and +0.6) look like generic redistribution rather than any change in what the sentence is about.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is search (+0.4): searching a room is exactly the raid script that relation one and relation three say is being dismantled, and it moves the wrong way, though only mildly and it can also be read intransitively with no object. Attack (+1.0) and steal (+0.4) are milder counterexamples to relation one, since both normally take an object; my defense is that they can stand objectless in a way that tie, drag and undress cannot, but this is a reading, not a fact about the numbers. Fire (-0.5) and unload (-0.5) cut the other way against relation one, since these are among the few falling verbs that need no stated object, which is why I filed them under relation three instead. Finally, the shout/yell fall against the scream rise is a swap between three near-synonyms, and treating it as a change of addressee rather than a lexical preference is the weakest inference in relation two.
result.notes: Two cautions about the arithmetic. The displayed words gain about 18.2 points and lose about 9.5, so this candidate set holds roughly 8.7 more points of mass under B than under A; some of the many small uniform rises on the B side may be that concentration rather than anything semantic, which is why I leaned on the falling block and on the four eliminations to zero, where direction cannot be an artifact of mass moving in. Second, the magnitudes are small in absolute terms (the largest single move is 3.1 points, from 3.6% to 6.7%), so the pattern is a coherent reading of many small movements rather than one decisive shift. The three relations are not independent: they are one story told through three word classes, namely that A's completions presuppose a fourth person in the room and B's do not. I want to be explicit that a sanitization or mildness reading would be wrong here: attack, destroy, fight, steal and scream all rise under B, and cry and pray rising alongside them is not a milder scene, only a differently populated one.

relations.name: Hosting script erased

residue.description: These are function words and phrase-openers rather than content completions, and although five of the six rise under B, which is consistent with the slot opening a longer frame instead of closing on a description, none of them tells you what the neighbours are said to be doing, and "up" is unresolvable because it could belong either to a late-hours reading or to an "up to something" reading that would sit on the opposite side of the second relation.

relations.name: Raid becomes assembly
relations.sentence: The verbs casting the room as a site of custody and search fall (beat, ask, interrogate, question, tie, drag, harass, torture, unload, check, pull), while the verbs casting it as a gathering of the three men among themselves rise (argue, discuss, chant, pray, sing, speak, chat), so the same entrance is rewritten from a raid into a meeting.

relations.name: Hands to mouths
relations.sentence: Every verb of physical contact with a body or an object loses probability (beat, hit, kick, cut, tear, tie, drag, pull, torture) and nearly everything that gains is produced with the voice (argue, discuss, speak, chant, sing, chat, pray, taunt), so the action moves from the hands to the mouth.

relations.name: Antagonism kept, rerouted
relations.sentence: Conflict does not leave the scene under B but changes medium: the struck-body verbs fall (beat, hit, kick, torture, harass) while hostility performed in speech or posture rises (argue, the largest single gain, together with fight, taunt and stare), so what is withdrawn is the contact rather than the aggression.

residue.description: frantically is an adverb rather than an act and make, set, get and cause are light verbs that carry no content until their missing complement arrives, so none of them names what happens in the room; clean, prepare and rummage are ordinary domestic or searching activity that rises under B without being either vocal or violent, and rummage is as compatible with a search of someone else's room as with tidying one's own.

result.counterexamples: The worst is ask, the second largest fall in the whole list at -2.3 and an entirely benign verb; question (-1.0) and check (-0.3) fall with it. result.reading: Under B the neighbours are more likely to feel threatened and unsafe and less likely to feel safe or safer, with the two security words that fall (-2.2 combined) almost exactly balanced by the two threat words that rise (+2.7 combined). Alongside that, two obligation words, compelled and obliged, rise together with nothing falling opposite them, and the pronoun "they" rises by +1.2 without being a content completion at all.

relations.name: security flips to threat
relations.sentence: The two words that place the neighbours in a state of safety lose probability under B while the two that place them under menace gain it, and the losses and gains are close to equal in size, so the shift reads as one axis being reversed rather than as a general spreading of probability.

relations.name: feeling becomes obligation
relations.sentence: Two words that reinterpret "felt" as the onset of a duty rather than an emotion both rise under B, with no comparable word falling on the A side, so this is an addition to the distribution rather than a substitution within it.

result.kind: the neighbours' construed footing toward the arrivals

residue.description: "they" is not a content completion but the start of a clausal complement ("felt they were..."), so its +1.2 rise says only that B prefers to postpone the affect into a following clause rather than commit to an adjective in the slot; because that clause would most often carry the same threat or obligation content, its direction is not independent evidence for either relation named above.

result.counterexamples: No word contradicts either relation: nothing on the A side belongs to the threat or obligation families, and nothing on the B side belongs to the security family. result.notes: The security relation is the strongest thing here because it moves in both directions at once and its two sides nearly cancel, which is harder to produce by noise than a one-sided rise; that is what keeps confidence from dropping to low despite the small point sizes. Confidence is not high because the whole visible mass in play is under three points and because the second-largest mover, "they", is uninterpretable as content. Note also that the fragment names a specific ethnic group, so the direction of the security flip is a claim about how that group's arrival is construed, and I have described it without treating it as evidence about anything beyond this one fragment under these two conditions.

Under A the three men are staged as agents of a raid; under B they are people in a room who talk, and even their hostility arrives as speech (curse, threaten, insult, harass) rather than as handling.

relations.name: raid script into talk script
relations.sentence: The verbs that describe a search party processing a room and its occupants (interrogate, search, take, tie, drag, pull, check) are uniformly more likely under A, while under B the same three men most likely argue, talk, speak, discuss or chat, so the largest movement in the distribution converts a detention scene into a conversation.

relations.name: hostility rekeyed as speech
relations.sentence: Aggression is not removed under B but changes channel: curse, threaten, insult, harass, scream and fight all rise, while what falls is physical handling (tie, drag, pull) together with yell, the plainest and least marked of the shouting verbs, so under B the men are hostile in words where under A they were hostile with hands.

relations.name: merely occupying the room
relations.sentence: Under B small amounts of probability accrue to simply being present as ordinary people in a room, praying, sitting or chatting, where A had preferred transitive errands with an implied object or task, give and work.

result.kind: which scene-script the subjects are cast into

All three moves are between 0.3 and 0.7 against leading shifts of 1.8 to 3.6, so they bend the relations rather than break them.

First, nothing is eliminated and nothing is created: every word retains a non-trivial probability under both conditions, the largest single move is 3.6 points, and no word goes to or from near zero. Second, the two blocks are unequal in length (13 against 11) and I have read no meaning into that; the reading rests on which words carry the largest movements, where the top of each block is unusually clean, four speech verbs up and two raid verbs down. result.reading: Almost all the movement is one word: "threatened" nearly doubles, taking +7.0 of a total shift whose next largest content item is +0.8, while the A side loses a scatter of small amounts across words about being unable to act (helpless, powerless, abandoned) and words about being under some duty or regret (obliged, obligated, sorry). Alongside that, the clause-opening function words (that, it, so) all rise, so B both concentrates on a single named emotion and more often postpones naming one at all.

relations.name: menace displaces impotence
relations.sentence: Under A the neighbours' feeling is spread across words for being unable to act or being left in a bad position, and under B that spread collapses into a single word naming an external danger, with two smaller security-vocabulary items following it.

relations.name: duty gives way to danger
relations.sentence: The words that make the feeling a matter of what the neighbours owe or regret toward someone else all fall under B, and none of the words that rise under B has that relational-moral sense at all.

relations.name: clause openers rise
relations.sentence: Under A the probability sits on single adjectives that complete the feeling immediately, while under B a sizeable share moves onto words that open a following clause instead, deferring whatever the feeling turns out to be.

result.kind: which register names the reaction, and whether it is named at all

residue.description: These are bare determiners whose eventual completion is not visible in the slot, so nothing about the direction of the shift can be read off them: "a" (+0.4) and "their" (+0.8) rise and "no" (-0.2) falls, but each could head a phrase of almost any affective colour.

result.counterexamples: Two items cut against the first relation. "safer" rises under B (+0.3), which a straightforward reading of B as intensified threat cannot accommodate, since the same condition raises both poles of the safety axis; the amount is small enough that it damages the relation only mildly, but it does show B is recruiting a security vocabulary rather than simply making things worse. More seriously, "uneasy" falls under B (-0.9) even though it belongs to the same danger register as "threatened" and "unsafe"; if B were shifting the whole threat vocabulary upward, "uneasy" should have moved with it. Its falling suggests the shift is toward one particular lexeme rather than toward a semantic field, which weakens the claim that the relation is about menace as such rather than about the word "threatened". "sorry" (-0.3) is small enough to carry little weight either way.
result.notes: The single +7.0 move dominates everything else here, so the honest description is mostly a description of one word; the A-side groupings are each built from moves of about a point or less and are correspondingly less secure. I have used the same A-side adjectives in relations one and three, since the same fall in the direct-adjective block is both a change of register and a change of syntactic commitment, and I could not separate the two from these numbers alone. Nothing in the data tells me which condition is which, and I have not assumed that the direction of the change is evaluative.

result.reading: The three largest moves by far are not emotion words at all: `that` (+8.5), `they` (+8.0) and `it` (+5.1), which together account for 21.6 of the 27.7 points gained across the whole B block, so under B the slot is overwhelmingly likely to open a reported clause ("felt that they...") rather than to be filled with a single adjective naming the neighbours' state. Underneath that structural move there is a smaller and more equivocal shift among the adjectives that remain: `threatened` and `alarmed` are the only state words to rise, while diffuse-discomfort words (`uneasy`, `uncomfortable`, `anxious`), both words asserting safety (`safe`, `safer`), and the whole "felt compelled/obliged/free to" infinitive frame fall.

relations.name: Clause displaces adjective
relations.sentence: Under B the slot is far more likely to open a subordinate clause or take a pronominal object about what was felt (that, they, it, what, some, and the intensifier very, which defers the adjective by one token) while nearly every predicate adjective that would name the neighbours' state outright loses probability, so the completion stops committing to a single emotion word in the slot itself.

relations.name: Threat replaces unease
relations.sentence: Among the words that still name a state, the only two to gain are the ones that specify an external danger with an implied agent behind it, while the vague-discomfort words fall and both words that would assert the neighbours were unharmed drop to near zero, so B sharpens an unspecific bad feeling into perceived menace and almost eliminates the reading in which nothing was wrong.

relations.name: Compulsion frame collapses
relations.sentence: The two single largest falls on the A side, together with a third word taking the same construction, are all continuations of "felt ___ to" (an obligation or permission to act rather than an emotion), and this deontic infinitive frame is almost wholly gone under B, its mass going to the clause-opening words instead.

result.kind: whether the feeling is named outright or deferred into a reported clause

residue.description: The runs of underscores are artifacts of the blanked-slot format rather than content completions of the fragment, and they move only slightly and in both directions; the remaining function words are alternative low-mass frames ("felt their", "felt an", "felt no", "felt for", "felt at", "felt there") that each fall by 0.2 to 0.9 as part of a general thinning of the tail, too small and too heterogeneous to attach to any of the named relations.</description>

result.counterexamples: The sharpest counterexample to the first relation is `as` (-1.6) together with `like` (-0.8): these open the "felt as if..." and "felt like they..." frames, which are themselves clausal, so B is not shifting to clausal complementation in general but specifically toward the bare "that/it/they" complement and away from the hedged or simile frame, which narrows the relation rather than refuting it. `very` (+1.4) cuts the other way within the same relation, since it is a pre-adjectival intensifier and its rise means B does still sometimes reach for an adjective, just one position later; this is mild but real, and it is also the reason `very` sits in the b_words of a relation whose story is that adjectives are losing. Against the second relation, `shocked` (-0.3) and `alarmed` (+0.5) are near-synonyms moving in opposite directions, which the threat reading cannot explain; both moves are small enough that this is a mild embarrassment rather than a contradiction. `proud` (-0.2) and `sorry` (-0.7) fit no threat/safety axis at all and are carried by the first relation only.
result.notes: Three qualifications on how much weight these will bear. First, the visible A-side losses total about 14.9 points against about 27.7 points of visible B-side gains, so roughly half the mass feeding `that`, `they` and `it` comes from words not shown in either block; any account built only on the listed A words is describing the smaller half of the transfer. Second, the confidence split is uneven across the relations and the single figure above averages them: the first relation rests on moves of 8.5, 8.0 and 5.1 and is not in doubt, whereas the second rests entirely on moves of 1.5 and 0.5 up against 0.7 and under down, which is the size range where the tail is unreliable, and I would call that one low on its own. What supports it is only that the direction is consistent across five independent words (both safety words and all three discomfort words down, both danger words up), not the size of any one of them. Third, membership overlaps deliberately: `uneasy`, `uncomfortable`, `anxious`, `safe` and `safer` appear in both the first and second relations because the first is about the grammatical slot they are losing and the second about which of them loses hardest, and `compelled`, `obliged` and `free` appear in both the first and third for the same reason. I have not treated the first relation as evidence that B is being evasive or the second as evidence about the direction of an attitude; the data given show a construction change with a smaller affective change riding on it, and the fragment's political content is not something these numbers can settle.

result.reading: The largest movements are all locative or deictic: outside +4.1, out +3.5, there +2.4, in +1.3, around +1.0, outdoors +0.8, with home, at, seen and together behind them. Nearly everything that falls is either a character adjective (nice, polite, kind, good) or a verb of household friction (fighting, complaining, throwing, late); the falls are small and diffuse where the rises are concentrated in one semantic place.

relations.name: Character to whereabouts
relations.sentence: Adjectives that would ascribe a settled trait or manner to the neighbors give way to words saying where they were located or how visibly present they were, so the predicate stops describing persons and starts reporting position.

relations.name: Friction to plain doings
relations.sentence: Participles whose choice implies a complaint from the other side of the wall recede while participles of ordinary sociable or working activity rise, so the same verb slot stops carrying a grievance.

relations.name: Adjective slot to particle slot
relations.sentence: The completion also changes grammatical shape: predicate adjectives that would close the sentence in a single word lose ground to bare prepositions and locative particles that leave the phrase open and expect a place to follow.

result.kind: character versus location as what gets predicated

residue.description: very and so are degree adverbs rather than content completions, and since each merely sets up an adjective that is not shown, their opposite small movements say nothing about what the sentence would have gone on to assert; cooking falls to zero but is a neutral domestic activity rather than a trait or a friction verb, so no relation here covers it.

result.counterexamples: very rises by +0.4 while presupposing exactly the evaluative adjective slot that relations one and three say is receding, though so falls by more than twice as much in the same class, so the contradiction is partly self-cancelling and small either way. cooking is eliminated (0.3% to 0.0%) even though it is a neutral domestic activity of the kind relation two says rises, and it is the only word fully removed. watching falls by 0.3 although it belongs to the observation and visibility family that relation one says gains. result.notes: Relations one and three rest on the four largest moves in the set, roughly eight points of locative rise against a largest single fall of 1.3, and I would call those high confidence on their own. Relation two rests entirely on moves of 0.5 or less and is the reason for the overall medium. Worth stating plainly: this is not a shift in valence. On levels: nothing is created from zero, though outdoors and seen quintuple from 0.2 to 1.0, and cooking is the only elimination. I have no information about which condition is which, and the fragment names an ethnic group, which is context I am deliberately not using to infer a direction.

result.reading: Under A the slot is filled almost entirely by a small set of positively valenced dispositional adjectives about how these neighbors behave toward the speaker (polite, friendly, nice, pleasant), and those four words alone account for about 22.5 of the roughly 31 points that leave A; several more of that register are driven to zero outright (cordial, helpful, welcoming, bringing). Under B that mass does not land on an opposite evaluation but disperses in half-point increments across twenty-seven words that mostly name observable activity, position and audibility (seen, out, in, busy, talking, quiet, staring, whispering, outside, together), with the single largest riser being the passive "seen."

relations.name: Praise traded for activity
relations.sentence: The words losing the most under A are dispositional adjectives evaluating the neighbors' manner toward the speaker, while the words gaining under B are participles and locative words naming what the neighbors were doing or where they were, so the completion shifts from an attribution of character to a report of behavior.

relations.name: Watched rather than met
relations.sentence: The A-side words place the neighbors in reciprocal contact with the speaker as people who greet, welcome and help, whereas the B-side risers place them at a distance as things observed and overheard, led by the passive "seen" and joined by staring, whispering, together, outside and there.

relations.name: Few words into many
relations.sentence: Roughly 72 percent of the probability leaving A sits in just four adjectives, while what arrives under B is spread so thinly that no word gains as much as five points and half the risers gain 0.6 or less, so the distribution changes shape as much as it changes vocabulary.

result.kind: judgment of character versus record of observed conduct

residue.description: These are not content completions of the slot but determiners, particles, degree modifiers and auxiliaries that open a longer clause rather than naming anything, so their movement records that B's continuations tend to run on past the single-adjective slot rather than telling us what B thinks the neighbors are; note that "a" at +2.7 is the fourth-largest gain under B, meaning a substantial share of B's gain is syntactic rather than semantic.

result.counterexamples: "quiet" (+1.8) and "silent" (+0.4) are the sharpest counterexamples, and they cut at the second relation: both rise under B and both are perfectly compatible with being good neighbors, so reading B's gains as surveillance is an interpretation of quiet-as-watchful rather than something the numbers force, and quiet is among B's larger movers. "curious" (+0.3) rises under B while being exactly the grammatical type (a disposition adjective) that relation one assigns to A, though its movement is small enough to dent rather than break the split. "complaining" (-0.3) falls under A despite being negative and unfriendly, so A is not cleanly "the positive block"; again the movement is small. "dressed" (+0.5) is an appearance-and-manner word close to A's evaluative register. Against the third relation, "seen" at +4.7 and "out" at +3.6 show B is not purely diffuse.
result.notes: The first relation I would give on its own as high confidence: the A side is unusually clean, four words carrying most of the change, all of one semantic and grammatical type, with seven words eliminated to 0.0 percent (cordial, helpful, bringing, welcoming, extremely, perfectly, eager). What lowers my overall confidence is the B side, which is dispersed enough that its character is a reading rather than a measurement. Three of its words are created from 0.0 percent (whispering, silent, singing) and the loudness axis rises at both poles simultaneously (quiet +1.8 and noisy +0.6, silent +0.4 and loud +0.5, whispering +0.6 and talking +2.0), which is not a valence shift and is better described as an increase in describing audible behavior at all. I have not assumed which condition is which, and nothing in the numbers tells me; the relations are stated as A-to-B differences and would read the same reversed. The two blocks are 28 and 20 words long, which I have ignored as instructed, but the mass is also asymmetric in a way I have not ignored: about 34 points arrive under B against about 31 leaving A, and A's top four carry 72 percent of its loss where B's top four carry 41 percent of its gain.

result.reading: Almost the entire difference is one word: friendly goes from 3.3% to 23.2%, a move seven times larger than anything else on the page, with the determiner "a" second at +8.5, which suggests B is also reshaping the grammar of the slot toward a predicate frame ("were always very friendly", "were always a ..."). Under A the mass sits in a thin tail of participles and prepositions saying what the neighbors were doing or where they were, including complaint verbs that B drives to exactly 0.0%; but B is not simply sweetening the slot, since good, happy, kind and welcome all fall under B while noisy, loud and arguing all rise.

relations.name: Collapse onto friendly
relations.sentence: Under B the descriptive slot concentrates on one canonical adjective of good neighborliness and its satellites, friendly alone taking nearly twenty points with pleasant, smiling, peaceful and the intensifier very behind it, while the generic warm adjectives A had spread mass across all fall, three of them to a tenth of a point or less.

relations.name: Grievance verbs zeroed
relations.sentence: The participles that would report these neighbors through a complaint heard across a wall are not merely reduced under B but eliminated, five of them landing at exactly 0.0% and the rest at 0.1-0.2%, while what rises in their place is close to the denial such a complaint would prompt.

relations.name: Deixis into predication
relations.sentence: A puts small amounts across bare prepositions and light participles that would carry the sentence on into a location or an ongoing activity, whereas B moves that mass into the frame of an attributed standing quality, raising the determiners and the intensifier that introduce an adjective or noun predicate.

result.kind: standing character attributed rather than activity observed

residue.description: Most of these are function words or light verbs whose actual content lies in a word not shown (making, causing, keeping, getting all wait on a following noun, so their movement cannot be read as a change in what is being said), and the rest are small domestic-activity terms (cooking, singing, outside, late, busy) that move under half a point in either direction and sit below the noise of a distribution whose largest single move is nearly twenty points.

result.counterexamples: Two sets cut against the relations. First, B raises several words of exactly the kind relation two says are being suppressed: noisy (+1.1), loud (+0.9), arguing (+0.6), smoking (+1.0) and playing (+2.8, the third-largest riser on the page). This does not overturn relation two, since those are the mild sensory versions and the accusatory verbs (screaming, banging, bothering, complaining) all go to 0.0%, but it does mean the suppression is graded by severity rather than by topic, and any reading of B as removing the neighbor-nuisance frame outright is wrong. Second, and more damaging to relation one, four positive adjectives move the other way: good (1.2 to 0.1), happy (0.6 to 0.0), kind (0.5 to 0.1) and welcome (0.4 to 0.2). B is not raising warmth in general; it is raising one specific formula and eliminating its near-synonyms, which is a different thing and would look identical if you only inspected the sign of the valence.
result.notes: Relation one is not really in doubt at +19.8; the confidence rating is dragged down by relations two and three, which rest on moves of one point or less and could be read as the tail thinning out mechanically once a single completion absorbs twenty points of mass. What survives that objection is the pattern of which words end at exactly 0.0% versus which merely shrink, and the fact that good, happy, kind and welcome fall while friendly rises, since simple renormalization would not select among near-synonyms that way. I have not assumed a direction of intervention or which condition is prior; the description holds either way round.

result.reading: Under B the distribution collapses onto a small template of neighborly character adjectives and their intensifiers: friendly gains almost eight points, with very, polite, so, kind, welcoming and pleasant rising behind it. What thins out under B is small in every individual case but broad in kind: gerunds and locatives that would have continued the sentence into observed activity (talking, working, hanging, playing, out, outside, around), plus suspicious as the single largest faller.

relations.name: Doing Yields To Being
relations.sentence: Continuations that would have described what the neighbors were seen doing or where they were (talking, working, hanging, playing, telling, out, outside, around) all lose probability under B, while the slot fills instead with stable dispositional adjectives (friendly, polite, kind, quiet, welcoming, pleasant), so the sentence turns from an observation of activity into an attribution of character.

relations.name: Warmth Crowds Wariness
relations.sentence: The one wary word in the field, suspicious, is the largest faller under B, and rude falls slightly as well, while the mass they and the rest of the A block give up is absorbed by warmth adjectives led by friendly, which alone gains more than the entire A block loses.

relations.name: Intensifier Slot Opens
relations.sentence: Degree words that postpone the adjective by one token, very and so, are the second and fourth largest gainers under B, while bare adjectives that would fill the slot directly (helpful, willing, quick) fall, which fits a shift toward an intensified praise frame of the form always very friendly rather than a plain predicate.

result.kind: attributed disposition versus observed activity

residue.description: The function words a and at are syntactic openings rather than content completions, and both move only slightly, so their rise says little beyond the general reshuffling of small probability mass; trying rises although it is a gerund like the ones that fall, and it is a hedge word (always trying to) that belongs to neither the activity group nor the character group cleanly.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is helpful, a plainly positive character adjective that falls under B (1.0 to 0.5) while friendly, polite, kind, welcoming and pleasant all rise, which shows the relation is not simply that positive words gain; willing behaves the same way at smaller size. This damages any pure valence reading but is compatible with the intensifier and template readings, since B is concentrating on a narrow set of neighborliness words rather than on positivity in general. Second, rude falls only 0.2 points, far less than suspicious at 0.8, so the wariness relation rests almost entirely on a single word and should not be read as a general suppression of negative traits. Third, trying rises 0.4 against the direction of the activity-gerund group, and quiet rises 1.0 although it is a descriptive rather than warm attribution, both mild strains rather than refutations given their size.
result.notes: The B side carries nearly all the magnitude here: friendly alone (+7.9) exceeds the sum of every fall, and very (+4.3), polite (+3.6), so (+2.5) and kind (+2.1) follow, whereas the largest single fall is suspicious at 0.8 and most A-side words move 0.2 or 0.3. So the confident statement is about concentration under B onto a warmth-plus-intensifier template; the story about what is being displaced is assembled from many small movements and is correspondingly weaker. Nothing is eliminated outright except working (0.3 to 0.0), and nothing is created from zero, so this is redistribution within an existing field rather than the appearance or removal of options. Confidence is medium rather than high because the direction of the B block is unambiguous while the composition of the A block is only loosely coherent and includes helpful, which runs against the reading.

result.reading: The fragment is a bare arrival ("Three Israelis came into the room and started to ___"), and the two conditions complete it as two different scenes: under A the room already contains someone the newcomers act upon, so the verbs are those of an armed search or detention (beat, shoot, interrogate, strip, torture, drag, rape, load), while under B the room is empty of anyone but the three, so the verbs are those of an occasion among themselves (talk, speak, chat, dance, laugh, unpack, pray). The movement is very lopsided in shape: the gains pile onto a handful of speech verbs, with talk, speak and chat alone taking about +32.9 points, while the losses are spread thinly across 41 words, none larger than -3.0, and 22 of them land at exactly 0.0%.

relations.name: Raid read as visit
relations.sentence: Under A the arrival is completed as a violent entry performed on people already present, with beat (3.0%), shoot (3.1%), kill, torture, assault, strip, drag and rape all live, and under B every one of those either vanishes to 0.0% or nearly so, while the same three men instead talk, speak, chat, dance, laugh, pray and eat.

relations.name: Speech loses its asymmetry
relations.sentence: Speech does not simply increase: the speech verbs in which the speaker holds power over the person addressed all fall (question -1.2, ask -0.8, interrogate -0.7, yell -0.2), while the reciprocal ones make the four largest rises on the panel (talk +15.0, speak +11.4, chat +6.5, argue +3.2, with discuss, explain and tell behind them), so the channel survives and only the direction of address is withdrawn.

relations.name: Bodies swapped for furniture
relations.sentence: The verbs that fall take an unnamed human patient (search, remove, strip, drag, tie, pull, examine, check, film), and the verbs that rise take the room and its contents instead (unpack, pack, clean, clear, fill, prepare, settle, set, light), so what changes is not only the force of the action but the sort of thing it is done to.

result.kind: which scene the arrival is read as staging

residue.description: These are light or purely deictic verbs whose content lives in a complement the fragment never supplies, so their movement cannot be read as being about anything in particular: take is the third-largest fall on the panel at -2.1 and is uninterpretable without knowing whether what was to be taken was a seat or a person, and the same holds for do, get, give, try, go, carry, move, run and roll, while study (+0.4) and sing (-0.3) move too little in either direction to attach to a group.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is argue at +3.2, the fourth-largest rise on the panel: a verb of open conflict becoming five times more likely refutes any reading of this as conflict or unpleasantness being removed, though it is consistent with the second relation, since arguing is something done between equals. Sing falls (-0.3) while dance, laugh and recite rise, which splits the festive group against itself, but the size is small enough that it barely counts. Against the first relation more seriously, a large block of the falls carries no violence at all: film (-0.8), move (-0.8), look (-0.5), do (-0.5), go (-0.3) and run (-0.2) drop alongside the assaults, which means the change cannot be described as harm being suppressed word by word, and this is why the relations are stated as a change of scene rather than a change of severity. Two rises are not predicted by any of the three relations and should be recorded as such: pray (+0.3) and recite (+1.0) introduce a devotional register that neither the raid frame nor a domestic one calls for, and smoke (+0.3) is not obviously part of any tidy scene.
result.notes: Three cautions on what I have and have not claimed. First, the two blocks are asymmetric in structure and not only in length: the rises are concentrated, with talk, speak and chat taking roughly +32.9 of about +45 total gained, while the falls are spread across 41 words with no single loss beyond -3.0, so under B the distribution is much more committed to a single continuation than under A is to any. Second, the printed values are rounded to one decimal, so a word shown at 0.0% has fallen below 0.05 rather than been demonstrably zeroed, and I have written "vanishes to 0.0%" in that sense only. Third, I have treated A and B as unlabeled conditions and have not assumed which is which, or that either is a baseline; the relations name a difference between two readings of the same fragment and would read identically if the arrow were reversed.
